title: Special Handloom and Handicraft Exhibition Themed ‘Vikas Aur Virasat’ Inaugurated by Union Minister Shri Giriraj Singh at IITF 2026
body_text: Shri Giriraj Singh, Hon’ble Union Minister of Textiles, Government of India , inaugurated the “Special Handloom & Handicraft Exhibition cum Sale” at the India International Trade Fair (IITF), Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi on 16 th November 2026. The inauguration took place in the august presence of Smt. Arti Kanwar, Additional Secretary, Smt. Amrit Raj, Development Commissioner Handicrafts, Sh. Rajiv Ashok, MD, NHDC (National Handloom Development Corporation Ltd) and other senior officials from the Ministry and NHDC. This year’s pavilion is themed “Vikas Aur Virasat” , celebrating India’s timeless craft legacy through a geographical journey across North, South, East and West —highlighting the unique handloom and handicraft traditions of different regions. The pavilion showcases India’s cultural diversity through four regional representations: North – Reflection & Ancestral Grace: Featuring traditional motifs of Ganesha, Ram Darbar and the luminous Banarasi weave, symbolising lineage and inherited excellence. South – Precision, Devotion & Sculptural Discipline: Showcasing Karnataka and Tamil Nadu’s mastery in wood, silk and metal crafts, along with the cosmic rhythm of Natraj. East – Memory, Continuity & the Handwoven Heartbeat: Highlighting the traditional weaving heritage of Odisha and Bengal, reflecting cultural identity and continuity. West – Radiance, Celebration & Desert Brilliance: Showcasing mirrorwork, Lippan art and carved wood, representing desert resilience and festive spirit.) Shri Giriraj Singh interacted with participating weavers and artisans after the inauguration formalities. He emphasized on the Government of India’s continuous efforts to strengthen the entire value chain—from raw material support to technology integration, design interventions and market linkages. He reiterated the Ministry’s commitment to expanding income and livelihood opportunities for weavers and craftspeople, reinforcing India’s leadership as the world’s largest and most sustainable handloom and handicraft ecosystem . The Union Minister of Textiles highlighted that development must go hand in hand with heritage, noting that handloom, handicrafts and jute have been an integral part of India's heritage for over 5,000 years. Emphasising their contribution to economic growth and employment generation, he said that the handloom and handicrafts sectors alone are associated with over one crore artisans, supporting millions of livelihoods both directly and indirectly. He further highlighted their significant contribution to the domestic market and exports, expressing confidence that sales at this year's International Trade Fair would reach new heights, with both domestic demand and export opportunities expected to grow in the coming years. The event, scheduled from 13th to 27th November 2026 , is open to the public from 10:00 AM to 7:30 PM in Hall No. 5, Ground Floor, Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. With 200 stalls representing 100 Handloom and 100 Handicraft artisans. Representing more than 21 States and Union Territories showcasing various types of  distinct crafts , the pavilion is managed by the National Handloom Development Corporation (NHDC) to provide direct market access to handloom weavers and handicraft artisans The textile theme pavilion also features distinguished master artisans, including 7 National Awardees, 3 State Awardees, 2 Sant Kabir Awardees, and more than 5 multiple award holders , with a total of 17 awardees from both the Handloom and Handicraft sectors. whose exceptional craftsmanship enriches the cultural experience of the pavilion and reflects the artistic excellence of India’s textile heritage. ***** RT/VN
